question: A 52-year-old patient who reported dyspnea of ​​medium effort for 6 months. He has not presented angina or syncopes. The physical examination and diagnostic tests show the existence of an average aortic transvalvular gradient of 55 mmHg and a calculated area of ​​0.7 cm2. Ejection fraction of 65%. The treatment that should be indicated to this patient is:

options.opa: Diuretics and more frequent controls by a specialist.
options.opb: In case of increasing dyspnea on exertion, a percutaneous dilatation of the aortic valve with a balloon catheter should be performed.
options.opc: Replacement of the aortic valve with a prosthesis / bioprosthesis.
options.opd: Replacement of the aortic valve by a homograft.
